problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav agents rely on a single limited, often occluded egocentric view, so target location estimation is poor. Prior assisted-navigation work with overhead views uses learned emergent communication with fixed vocabularies and simple targets, not free-form natural language.
motivation: Overhead or monitoring cameras are widely available and can give a global view containing the target, so a ground robot could use them for assistance. Natural-language communication between VLM-equipped heterogeneous agents is little explored. It is unclear whether simply following the assistant's guidance helps, and how communication quality (hallucination) affects navigation.
key_idea: Let a VLM-equipped ground agent and a static overhead agent exchange free-form generative communication before acting, and let the ground agent selectively decide whether to follow the overhead agent's suggested action or explore independently.
insight: Blindly following the overhead agent's advice (Cooperative Action) hurts, dropping to 9.00 OSR and 8.50 SPL at C_len=5 versus the 22.00 and 21.50 no-communication baseline. Selective Action lifts these to 32.00 and 29.15. Preemptive hallucination (the dialogue assumes the ground agent has already moved) grows with communication length, from 48.2% to 81.6% in Cooperative Action, while the selective cooperation rate falls (23.2 to 18.9). This suggests the ground agent learns to distrust hallucinated summaries, so retaining independent exploration matters even when the helper sees the target.
method: Assisted ObjectNav setup: a dynamic Ground Agent (GA, egocentric RGB) and a static Overhead Agent (OA, global top view containing the target), both driven by the same VLM (GPT-4-turbo / GPT-4V).

Communication phase C: OA and GA alternate free-form dialogue for C_len turns (1, 3, 5); the OA asks about the GA's surroundings and the dialogues are concatenated into a Generative Communication (GC) summary.
Cooperative Action: the OA/LLM reads the GC and the overhead image, outputs one discrete action (MoveAhead/MoveBack/RotateLeft/RotateRight/DoNothing), and the GA executes it unconditionally.
Selective Action: the GA VLM is shown the suggested action and its own image and answers Yes/No; on No it falls back to the no-communication VLM policy from its egocentric view.
Baselines: No Comm. (GA VLM acts alone from its egocentric view) and Random action selection. An extra ablation lets the GA first decide whether to communicate at all (selective communication).
GC trait analysis: preemptive hallucination H_PE (GPT-4 classifier), ghost-object hallucination H_GO (vocabulary overlap), cooperation rate CR, and dialogue similarity DS (BERT cosine).
Real-world prompt finetuning: environment-specific prompt edits (orange marker on the Turtlebot, note about floor light reflections) reduce OA localization and reflection hallucinations.

setting.backbone: GPT-4-turbo (frozen) in sim; GPT-4V (frozen) in real world; InstructBLIP and LLaVA-1.5 tried and rejected
setting.observation: GA: monocular egocentric RGB; OA: static overhead RGB camera (7.25 m height in sim, GoPro in real world); action history and result feedback given in prompts
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead/MoveBack 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 90°, DoNothing; 10 steps per episode
setting.simulator: RoboTHOR / AI2-THOR with ProcTHOR rooms; real Turtlebot 2
setting.privileged: Overhead camera view containing the target (the assistive setup); prompts include the shortest-path distance to the target after each action; a static overhead viewpoint is assumed

numbers_note: Custom RoboTHOR/ProcTHOR evaluation on 100 rooms, not a standard benchmark. No standard benchmark numbers are reported, and the real-world experiments are qualitative only. The abstract's 7.65% SPL gain does not match Table 1's +8.0 for C_len=5.
results: Selective Action with C_len=5 reaches 32.00 OSR and 29.15 SPL, versus 22.00/21.50 for the no-communication VLM baseline and 15.00/11.69 for random. Fully cooperative execution falls below the baseline at every C_len (9.00 OSR / 8.50 SPL at C_len=5). Preemptive hallucination rises with communication length and correlates with cooperative-action performance.
limitations: Tiny, non-standard evaluation (100 ProcTHOR rooms, 10 steps, single-instance targets, single VLM), and absolute success rates stay low (32% OSR at best)
Only a one-to-one dialogue with a single static overhead agent; VLMs localize poorly from the overhead view and hallucinate, and real-world results are qualitative with hand-tuned prompts
Episodes on which GPT-4-turbo raised errors (e.g., plain wall views) were excluded from evaluation
